ADDICTION MEDICINE NOTE   Date: 2025-07-17
35M, emergency room encounter with follow-up in the outpatient program.

S:
Patient was seen in the emergency room and is reviewed here for continuity of his outpatient program care. He reports cravings that have been moderate over the past two weeks, worse after long shifts. He attends group twice weekly and individual counseling on Tuesdays and has kept most appointments. He works as a warehouse associate. He could not complete 4 of his scheduled shifts last month because of symptoms. No shortness of breath. Sleep is improving, about 6 hours a night. Appetite is good. Lives with his partner, who is supportive of his treatment. Taking medications as prescribed.

O:
BP 124/78, HR 80, RR 14, Temp 98.3 F, SpO2 99% on room air. Weight 170 lb, stable.
General: alert, cooperative, calm appearing.
HEENT: pupils equal and reactive.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Skin: no track marks or lesions.
Psych: linear thought process, good insight, engaged and future-oriented.
Labs (drawn in the ED): comprehensive metabolic panel within normal limits, urine drug screen reviewed with patient.

A/P:
1. Psychoactive substance dependence, active, engaged in outpatient treatment. Continue group and individual counseling and current medication-assisted treatment. Reviewed a relapse-prevention plan and strategies for high-stress shifts. Provided program crisis line information and confirmed the next appointment.
2. Supportive care: reinforced sleep routine and stress-management techniques. Coordinated with the case manager to align counseling times with his work schedule.
3. Function and work: symptoms are affecting his ability to keep regular shifts. Discussed documentation to support a steady return to full hours.

Return to the program in 1 week, sooner if cravings escalate or he feels unsafe.
